titleEn: Churchill Club: An Evening with Elon Musk
titleZh: 丘吉尔俱乐部：与埃隆·马斯克共度一晚
summaryEn: A wide-ranging 2009 Churchill Club evening with Elon Musk on entrepreneurship, the founding of SpaceX and Tesla, and the thinking behind betting his PayPal fortune on rockets and electric cars.
summaryZh: 2009年丘吉尔俱乐部的一场内容广泛的晚间活动，埃隆·马斯克谈论创业、SpaceX和Tesla的创立，以及他为何决定将自己的PayPal财富押在火箭和电动汽车上。

segments.textEn: Hello everyone, welcome. My name is Karen Tucker. I'm CEO and board member of the Churchill Club. And tonight we present an evening with Elon Musk in conversation with Michael Malone, Elon and Mike, thank you very much for being here with us tonight. And I would also like to thank Microsoft for hosting this program this evening. Before we get started, let me mention some of our upcoming events. First, on Tuesday, April 21, it's virtualization.
segments.textZh: 大家好，欢迎各位。我叫卡伦·塔克。我是丘吉尔俱乐部的首席执行官兼董事会成员。今晚，我们将呈现埃隆·马斯克与迈克尔·马隆对谈之夜。埃隆和迈克，非常感谢你们今晚来到这里与我们相聚。我还要感谢微软为今晚的活动提供场地。在开始之前，请允许我介绍一下我们即将举办的活动。首先，4月21日星期二，主题是虚拟化。

segments.textEn: What's next? Six leading experts will talk about trends and the next generation of this hot technology area. And then Next, on Thursday, April 23rd, we present a Women Tech Executive Roundtable. What's top of mind in 2009 with an all star cast including Sheryl Sandberg from Facebook. And on April 27th we have a program about executive leadership style and its effect on business performance. The panel will include Bill Campbell, Chairman of Intuit and others.
segments.textZh: 接下来是什么？6位顶尖专家将讨论这个热门技术领域的发展趋势和下一代技术。然后，接下来在4月23日星期四，我们将举办一场女性科技高管圆桌会议。2009年最受关注的是什么，嘉宾阵容群星荟萃，包括来自Facebook的谢丽尔·桑德伯格。4月27日，我们将举办一场关于高管领导风格及其对企业绩效影响的活动。嘉宾小组将包括Intuit董事长比尔·坎贝尔等人。

segments.textEn: You can look for that on ChurchillClub.org this week. And on May 7, it's our 2009 CIO agenda, including the CIOs of Home Depot, Baxter, among others. An incredible group. Should be an interesting program. This too we'll post on the website this week. And last but not least, it is our most anticipated program of the year, the Top 10 Tech Trends event on Wednesday, May 20th. And this year we have Vinod Khosla, Ram Shiram, Steve Jurvetson and Joe Schoendorf will be making their predictions with high audience participation.
segments.textZh: 本周你可以在ChurchillClub.org上查找相关信息。5月7日，是我们的2009年首席信息官议程，嘉宾包括家得宝、百特等公司的首席信息官。阵容非常了不起。应该会是一场很有意思的活动。本周我们也会把它发布到网站上。最后但同样重要的是，这是我们今年最受期待的活动，即5月20日星期三举行的十大科技趋势活动。今年，维诺德·科斯拉、拉姆·施里拉姆、史蒂夫·尤尔韦特松和乔·舍恩多夫将在观众高度参与的情况下作出他们的预测。

segments.textEn: So if you haven't yet made your reservation, please be sure to do that. Just a note about the club for over 23 years the Churchill Club has been the leading forum for the Bay Area business and technology community. Presenting Presenting what's new? What's next? What matters most? We are a nonprofit member supported group and so if you are not a member and you enjoy tonight's program, we hope that you will consider joining us and we make it easy for you to do so Simply just visit ChurchillClub.org and go through the steps.
segments.textZh: 所以，如果你还没有预订，请务必预订。简单介绍一下本俱乐部，23年多来，丘吉尔俱乐部一直是湾区商业和科技界的领先论坛。呈现 呈现什么是新事物？接下来是什么？什么最重要？我们是一个由会员支持的非营利团体，所以如果你还不是会员，并且喜欢今晚的活动，我们希望你能考虑加入我们；我们也让加入变得很容易，只需访问ChurchillClub.org并按照步骤操作即可。

segments.textEn: Now I'm pleased to introduce our moderator, Michael Malone. Mike has had a most impressive career having covered Silicon Valley and high tech for more than 25 years. He has written for the Wall Street Journal, Economist, Fortune, the New York Times, Forbes, ASAP and earlier the San Jose Mercury News. He wrote or co wrote a dozen books, he hosted three public television interview programs series and most recently he co produced a PBS miniseries called the New Heroes about social entrepreneurs.
segments.textZh: 现在，我很高兴介绍我们的主持人迈克尔·马隆。迈克拥有令人印象极为深刻的职业生涯，报道硅谷和高科技领域已有25年多。他曾为《华尔街日报》《经济学人》《财富》《纽约时报》《福布斯》《ASAP》撰稿，更早以前还曾为《圣何塞信使报》撰稿。他独著或合著了12本书，主持过3档公共电视访谈系列节目，最近还联合制作了一部名为《新英雄》的PBS迷你剧，讲述社会企业家。

segments.textEn: When I asked Mike for something about him that doesn't appear in his bio, he admitted that he was nearly expelled from Santa Clara University because he used a certain obscenity. I believe he said it contained 12 letters in his school paper column. I'm sure that wasn't the first time that Mike stirred things up, and I trust that it will not be the last either. So let's give a warm welcome to respected journalist and author Mike Malone.
segments.textZh: 当我请迈克说一件他个人简介里没有的事时，他承认自己差点被圣克拉拉大学开除，因为他使用了某个脏话。我记得他说，那个词有12个字母，出现在他为校报撰写的专栏里。我确信那不是迈克第一次掀起波澜，我也相信那不会是最后一次。那么，让我们热烈欢迎备受尊敬的记者兼作家迈克·马隆。

segments.textEn: Good evening, everybody. Looks like we have a pretty full house. Recognize a lot of faces and I promise not to or try not to use that 12 letter word tonight. Elon might, but I'll try not to. I hope all of you had a chance to take a look at the Tesla Roadster sitting out there in the parking lot. It was the one behind the orange cones that look very different from all the rest of the cars out there. If you didn't get a chance, try to beat Elon out of here tonight and go take a look at it or at least watch them tear out of the parking lot silently.
segments.textZh: 大家晚上好。看来现场几乎坐满了。我认出了很多面孔，而且我保证今晚不说，或者尽量不说那个有12个字母的词。埃隆可能会说，但我会尽量不说。希望大家都有机会看一看停在外面停车场里的那辆Tesla Roadster。就是橙色锥桶后面的那辆，看起来和外面的其他所有汽车都很不一样。如果你没来得及看，今晚争取赶在埃隆之前离开这里，去看一眼，或者至少看看他们如何悄无声息地冲出停车场。

segments.textEn: So allow me to do an introduction, sir. We've known each other a long time.
segments.textZh: 那么，请允许我作个介绍，先生。我们认识很久了。

segments.textEn: We have inner Churchill Club. Is 12 letters.
segments.textZh: 我们有内部丘吉尔俱乐部。是12个字母。

segments.textEn: Oh, yes, it is. Oh my goodness. I was just thinking it was 20. It's hard to believe. It was 28 years ago that Rich Karlgard and Tony Perkins showed me a plan for this. And it was about just a few years before I was shown the plan for ebay. And in both cases I said, I just don't think it's going to work.
segments.textZh: 哦，是的，确实如此。哦，我的天哪。我刚才还以为是20。很难相信。那是28年前，里奇·卡尔加德和托尼·珀金斯向我展示了这个计划。那大约是在有人向我展示eBay计划的几年前。在这两种情况下，我都说，我就是觉得这行不通。

segments.textEn: That's crazy.
segments.textZh: 太疯狂了。

segments.textEn: No, it's just crazy. So let me introduce you. 37 year old Elon Musk was born and raised in South Africa, but left home at age 17 to make his way in the world, living on as little as $1 per day. He eventually made his way to the Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania, where he earned bachelor's degrees in economics and physics. Musk then attended Stanford's graduate program in high energy physics, where he lasted exactly two days before dropping out to form a company with his brother.
segments.textZh: 不，这就是很疯狂。那么让我来介绍你。37岁的埃隆·马斯克在南非出生并长大，但17岁时离开家乡，到世界上闯荡，每天只靠低至1美元生活。他最终进入宾夕法尼亚大学沃顿商学院，获得经济学和物理学学士学位。随后，马斯克进入斯坦福大学的高能物理研究生项目，他在那里正好待了2天，之后便退学，与兄弟共同创办了一家公司。

segments.textEn: That company, Zip2, was sold for $300 million. Musk then founded exp.com, an online financial services company. It eventually became PayPal, of which Elon was the largest shareholder. PayPal, as we all know, was purchased by eBay for $1.5 billion in 2002. When he graduated from Wharton, Elon determined the three important areas where he wanted to make a contribution was the Internet, clean energy space. And with PayPal, Tesla Motors, SpaceX, and SolarCity, he has done just that and in the process made himself one of the most celebrated entrepreneurs on the planet.
segments.textZh: 那家公司Zip2以3亿美元售出。随后，马斯克创立了在线金融服务公司exp.com。它最终成为PayPal，而埃隆是其最大股东。众所周知，PayPal于2002年被eBay以15亿美元收购。从沃顿商学院毕业时，埃隆确定了自己希望作出贡献的3个重要领域，即互联网、清洁能源、太空。通过PayPal、Tesla Motors、SpaceX和SolarCity，他恰恰做到了这一点，并在此过程中使自己成为全球最负盛名的企业家之一。

segments.textEn: Ladies and gentlemen, Elon Musk.
segments.textZh: 女士们、先生们，埃隆·马斯克。

segments.textEn: So let's begin with the topic of greatest interest to the audience here tonight. I assume, Tesla Motors. Okay, where's the company at right now? Where do orders stand?
segments.textZh: 那么，让我们从今晚在场观众最感兴趣的话题开始。我想，是Tesla Motors。好，公司目前处于什么状况？订单情况如何？

segments.textEn: Oh, Mike, I don't know what to tell you. It's been rough. No, I'm just kidding. It's actually.
segments.textZh: 哦，迈克，我不知道该怎么跟你说。一直很艰难。不，我只是在开玩笑。实际上。

segments.textEn: It's actually been. It's been pretty good. In fact, really quite a contrast to the rest of the auto business. We're sold out, first of all, for the Tesla Roads to the sports car. We're sold out through the end of October, and I think probably within two or three months will be actually sold out of all 2009 production for the Roadster.
segments.textZh: 实际上一直都。一直都相当不错。事实上，与汽车行业的其他部分形成了非常鲜明的对比。首先，我们的 Tesla Roads to 跑车已经售罄。我们一直到10月底的车都已售罄，而且我认为可能在2或3个月内，Roadster 2009年的全部产量实际上都会售罄。

segments.textEn: Is this for the standard roadster or the. Or the advanced version?
segments.textZh: 这是标准版Roadster，还是那个。还是高级版本？

segments.textEn: Well, we do have a Roadster Sport coming out, which is a, you know, for those for whom the roadster. The Roadster isn't fast enough.
segments.textZh: 嗯，我们确实将推出一款 Roadster Sport，也就是，你知道，对于那些觉得 Roadster。觉得 Roadster 还不够快的人。

segments.textEn: Right.
segments.textZh: 对。

segments.textEn: There's the Roadster Sport.
segments.textZh: 还有 Roadster Sport。

segments.textEn: How fast is that one?
segments.textZh: 那款有多快？

segments.textEn: Now, that'll do 0 to 60 in 3.7 seconds. As fast as almost any.
segments.textZh: 那么，它从0加速到60需要3.7秒。几乎和任何一款一样快。

segments.textEn: It's like a nice CBM laid over on the side.
segments.textZh: 就像一台不错的 CBM 侧放着。

segments.textEn: Yeah, it's ridiculously fast.
segments.textZh: 是的，快得离谱。

segments.textEn: Now, how are the orders for that? Good.
segments.textZh: 那么，那款车的订单情况如何？不错。

segments.textEn: Actually, I haven't looked at the latest orders for the Roadster Sport, and people actually have an opportunity to upgrade their car to the Roadster Sport that are getting their car after, I think, late June or July. And what we're finding is a lot of people are choosing to upgrade their car to the Sport package. So I actually don't have an exact number for you, but anecdotally, it seems to be doing very well.
segments.textZh: 实际上，我还没有看 Roadster Sport 的最新订单，而且我想，那些在6月底或7月以后提车的人实际上有机会把自己的车升级为 Roadster Sport。我们发现，很多人都选择把自己的车升级到 Sport 套件。所以我确实没有一个确切数字可以告诉你，但从一些个别情况来看，它似乎卖得非常好。

segments.textEn: Now, The Roadster is 109,000, is that right?
segments.textZh: 那么，Roadster 是109,000，对吗？

segments.textEn: Yeah.
segments.textZh: 对。

segments.textEn: And the race sport's 139,000. Do I have that right?
segments.textZh: 而竞赛运动版是139,000。我说得对吗？

segments.textEn: Well, the price to customers is actually, in terms of a comparison price that's relevant for comparing it to a Porsche or something like that is actually about $98,000. And the reason for that is if you buy an electric car, you get a $7,500 federal tax rebate. Even if you're an AMT, it applies to everyone. And then you don't pay the gas guzzler tax, which is somewhere in the order of $3,000. So effectively $12,000 discount.
segments.textZh: 嗯，对顾客来说，实际上就相关的比较价格而言，也就是拿它与保时捷或类似车型比较时，实际上大约是98,000美元。原因是，如果你购买电动汽车，就能获得7,500美元的联邦税收抵免。即使你适用 AMT，这也适用于所有人。而且你不用缴纳高油耗汽车税，这笔税大约为3,000美元。所以实际上相当于12,000美元的折扣。

segments.textEn: Yeah, you're roughly. And it depends on which car you compare it against, because the gas cost of tax does vary, but it's somewhere between a 9 to $12,000 discount relative to a gasoline sports car. So in effect, you're talking about a car that's just under $100,000 as a base price. And then the sport package is another $20,000 on top of that. And that's equivalent to going from, you know, a 911 to a 911 Turbo or something, you know, that kind of thing.
segments.textZh: 是的，大致如此。而且这取决于你拿它和哪款车比较，因为汽油成本税确实有所不同，但相对于汽油跑车，折扣大约在9到12,000美元之间。所以实际上，你说的是一款基础价格略低于100,000美元的汽车。然后 Sport 套件要在此基础上再加20,000美元。这相当于从，你知道，911升级到911 Turbo之类的，你知道，就是那种情况。

segments.textEn: Now, if I were to order one right now, if anybody in the audience wants to order one right now, raise your hands. I will take orders. I mean, there you go. If somebody out here were to order one right now, what would it take? What's the deposit and what's the delivery date?
segments.textZh: 那么，如果我现在订一辆，如果现场观众中有人想现在订一辆，请举手。我可以接受订单。我是说，你看。如果现场有人现在订一辆，需要怎么做？订金是多少，交付日期又是什么时候？

segments.textEn: So we're actually reducing our deposit requirements on the Roadster. And previously we'd used the deposits to provide funding for the company, and that was an acknowledged thing. We said, look, we car companies are very capital intensive, so in order to make this doable or more doable, we're going to take deposits. They'll be at risk. People should recognize that. And then the advantage is that they get one of the first cars.
segments.textZh: 所以我们实际上正在降低 Roadster 的订金要求。此前我们一直用订金为公司提供资金，而且这是明确告知过的事情。我们说，听着，我们汽车公司是资本非常密集的，所以为了让这件事可行，或者更可行，我们将收取订金。这些订金将面临风险。人们应该认识到这一点。而好处是，他们能拿到最早的一批车。

segments.textEn: And we actually got a lot of people who sign up to that, but we don't really need that anymore. So we're actually going to reduce the deposit down to, I think, $9,900, and then you pay the balance just at start of production, which is a couple months prior to delivery.
segments.textZh: 而且实际上有很多人报名接受了这个安排，但我们现在其实不再需要这样做了。所以我们实际上会把订金降到，我想，9,900美元，然后你只需在开始生产时支付余款，而开始生产是在交付前两个月。

segments.textEn: Now, did you find any impact on the orders with the falling gas prices? We saw what happened with Prius. I mean, you can go to Cityvale and entire supermarket parking lots are filled with unsold Priuses. Did that affect you guys at all?
segments.textZh: 那么，油价下跌对订单有任何影响吗？我们看到了 Prius 的遭遇。我是说，你可以去 Cityvale，那里整个超市停车场都停满了卖不出去的 Prius。这对你们有任何影响吗？

segments.textEn: You know, I don't think that was a huge impact because most people aren't buying the $100,000 sports car because of the, you know, to save money on gas.
segments.textZh: 你知道，我不认为那产生了巨大影响，因为大多数人购买那辆100000美元的跑车，并不是为了，你知道，节省汽油费。

segments.textEn: It's more geek love than it is cheap gas.
segments.textZh: 与其说是廉价汽油，不如说是极客之爱。

segments.textEn: Yeah, I was more worried about how that would affect sales for our sedan, which we just unveiled a few weeks ago.
segments.textZh: 是的，我更担心的是，这会如何影响我们几周前刚刚发布的轿车的销量。

segments.textEn: We'll talk about that in a moment, but keep going. Yeah,
segments.textZh: 我们待会儿会谈到这个，不过请继续。是的，

segments.textEn: but I don't think that's been a key impact on roads to sales. I think certainly the economy as a whole and the implosion of people's net worths has had an effect on new roads to sales. And we're fortunate that we do have a significant backlog going out six months.
segments.textZh: 但我认为那并不是对道路销量产生关键影响的因素。我认为，整体经济状况以及人们净资产的崩塌，肯定对新道路销量产生了影响。而幸运的是，我们确实有大量积压订单，已经排到了6个月以后。

segments.textEn: But I wouldn't say gas prices have had a big effect on the road stuff.
segments.textZh: 但我不会说汽油价格对道路方面产生了很大影响。

segments.textEn: Now, being in the car business, you have to be asked, are you taking any federal money, you know, and are you worried about your job security if you are?
segments.textZh: 现在，既然从事汽车行业，就必须问你：你们有没有拿任何联邦资金，你知道，如果拿了，你担不担心自己的职位保障？

segments.textEn: Well, you know, I don't have to worry about My compensation, my compensation currently is a dollar. So I'd be happy to cut that in half for the federal government if they do give us a loan. But actually we've taken no government money at all thus far. Some people out there think we have and we haven't. Now we do aspire to get a government loan under the, what's called the ATVM program. It's the Advanced Technology Vehicle Manufacturing program.
segments.textZh: 嗯，你知道，我不必担心我的薪酬，我目前的薪酬是1美元。所以，如果联邦政府确实给我们贷款，我很乐意把薪酬减半。但事实上，迄今为止，我们完全没有拿过任何政府资金。外面有些人以为我们拿过，但我们没有。现在，我们确实希望根据所谓的 ATVM 计划获得政府贷款。那是先进技术车辆制造计划。

segments.textEn: That's from the doe.
segments.textZh: 那是美国能源部提供的。

segments.textEn: That's from the doe. It's not bailout money. And it was, this was, this program was done before there was need for ballot money. This legislation was written about 18, started writing it about 18 months ago and it got, finally got approved by Congress last year sometime I think late last year. So. And this is before a vomit. So this isn't stimulus money, this isn't bailout money. This is actually something that originated in the Senate Energy Committee because they felt it was a matter of national security for and environmental obviously environmentally important for the United States to accelerate its transition away from oil for all the obvious reasons that it's damaging.
segments.textZh: 那是美国能源部提供的。它不是救助资金。而且它……这个计划是在需要选票资金之前就制定的。这项立法大约是18……大约18个月前开始起草的，最终在去年某个时候获得了国会批准，我想是去年年底。所以。而且这是在一次呕吐之前。所以这不是刺激资金，也不是救助资金。这实际上是一项源自参议院能源委员会的举措，因为他们认为，对美国而言，加速摆脱石油的转型事关国家安全，而且显然对环境也很重要，原因显而易见，它具有破坏性。

segments.textEn: It's obviously very damaging to the environment. segments.textZh: 所以，就X大奖而言，有汽车X大奖，有面向低成本基因测序的基因组学X大奖。还有Google月球X大奖，SpaceX正试图通过提供……来帮上一点忙。实际上，我们唯一提供折扣的发射就是Google月球X大奖的发射。而且，是的，那里正在发生很多事情，我认为这是一个很好的模式。应该得到更多仿效。

segments.textEn: DARPA did a great example of a prize thing with the DARPA Grand Challenge. That was there's DARPHA Grand Challenge, DARPHA Urban Challenge for Autonomous vehicles. That's got to be one of the highest bang for buck items that DARPHA has ever done. Because I guarantee if you made that like a DoD contractor and had like, you know, Lockheed and Raytheon and all the usual suspects bet on it. It would have been like $2 billion and they'd still be working on it, you know.
segments.textZh: DARPA通过DARPA大挑战赛，为大奖这种做法树立了一个很好的范例。那是有DARPHA大挑战赛、面向自动驾驶车辆的DARPHA城市挑战赛。那肯定是DARPHA做过的投入产出比最高的项目之一。因为我敢保证，如果你把它变成一个国防部承包项目，让，比如说，你知道，洛克希德、雷神以及所有那些老面孔参与竞标。它就会耗资20亿美元，而且他们现在还会在做，你知道。

segments.textEn: So anyway, I think there's a lot of room for prizes and it should be more often.
segments.textZh: 所以无论如何，我认为大奖还有很大的施展空间，应该更频繁地采用。

segments.textEn: One more question then. I have one.
segments.textZh: 那再问一个问题。我有一个。

segments.textEn: Given the range of technologies and areas you've touched, I'm curious what your take on robotics is. It almost seems like on robotics. On robotics, exactly. It seems close enough to what you've done, but I haven't heard you talk about it. Well, you know, Tesla does use robotics to a limited extent in its production today, particularly on the battery pack side because you've got so many cells, almost 7,000 cells, that some robotic assistance is important in making the battery pack.
segments.textZh: 鉴于你涉足过如此广泛的技术和领域，我很好奇你对机器人技术有什么看法。机器人技术几乎看起来像是。对机器人技术。对，正是机器人技术。它似乎和你所做的事足够接近，但我没听你谈过它。嗯，你知道，Tesla如今确实在生产中有限度地使用机器人技术，尤其是在电池包这方面，因为电芯太多了，将近7,000个电芯，所以在制造电池包时，一些机器人辅助非常重要。

segments.textEn: And we'll soon see a lot more of that as Tesla scales up. So robotics makes a big. It's great for mass manufacturing, for space exploration. Obviously we've seen great evidence paid by robotics as well with the Mars Exploration Rovers.
segments.textZh: 随着Tesla扩大规模，我们很快就会看到更多这类应用。所以机器人技术有很大的。它非常适合大规模制造，也适合太空探索。显然，我们也已经从火星探测车那里看到了机器人技术所付出的有力证据。

segments.textEn: And there's a really big rover going called Mars Science Laboratory and that was supposed to launch soon, but it's going to be a couple years before that goes. That's about the size of like a Volkswagen.
segments.textZh: 还有一个非常大的探测车项目正在推进，名叫火星科学实验室，它本来应该很快发射，但还要过几年才能成行。它大约有一辆大众汽车那么大。

segments.textEn: So I mean, I think there's a lot of room for robotics in a lot of fields and that'll increase and continue in both automotive and space and other areas.
segments.textZh: 所以，我的意思是，我认为机器人技术在许多领域都有很大的施展空间，而且它在汽车、太空和其他领域都会增长并持续发展。

segments.textEn: But at the end of the day, you know, I think we still need to make life multi planetary. It can't just be sort of sending droids out there.
segments.textZh: 但归根结底，你知道，我认为我们仍然需要让生命成为多行星物种。不能只是把机器人送到那里去。

segments.textEn: I'm pro life in that sense. So I think robotic asteroids and robotic preparation.
segments.textZh: 从这个意义上说，我支持生命。所以我认为机器人小行星和机器人准备工作。

segments.textEn: But we also need life going beyond Earth as well. I was just curious from a perspective of making people's lives better.
segments.textZh: 但我们也需要让生命走出地球。我只是想从改善人们生活的角度了解一下。

segments.textEn: I was just curious if that is an area that you thought about going through in a nanosecond. I haven't really thought about robotics personally, but just not to say that I don't think there are lots of things that could be automated and where there could be robots that help people in their daily lives. You know, I'm sure there'll be a continued expansion of the whole iRobot type thing beyond vacuum cleaning.
segments.textZh: 我只是好奇，你是否曾在一纳秒间想过要涉足那个领域。我个人并没有真正思考过机器人技术，但这并不是说我认为没有许多事情可以自动化，也不是说不能有机器人帮助人们处理日常生活。你知道，我相信整个iRobot式的东西会继续扩展，超越吸尘这一用途。

segments.textEn: So yeah, yeah, I think it's a great area.
segments.textZh: 所以，是的，是的，我认为这是一个很棒的领域。

segments.textEn: I have one last question for you. I followed your career for a long time, known you for a long time. Yeah, you know, for many, many years. You were very, you were very successful, but largely anonymous.
segments.textZh: 我还有最后一个问题要问你。我关注你的职业生涯很久了，也认识你很久了。是的，你知道，很多很多年。你非常，你非常成功，但基本上默默无闻。

segments.textEn: Yeah, you know, I, for a long time, right. I was underground.
segments.textZh: 是的，你知道，我，很长一段时间，对。我一直默默无闻。

segments.textEn: I've seen you walk, you could walk the streets of Oxford and Nobody knew who you were. I saw you.
segments.textZh: 我见过你走在街上，你可以走在牛津的街头，却没人知道你是谁。我见过你。

segments.textEn: I think I could still do that, by the way.
segments.textZh: 顺便说一句，我觉得我现在仍然可以那样做。

segments.textEn: Well, but less and less in the last couple years, you've become increasingly a public figure, a celebrity, and your name starts popping up now in gossip pages and websites and that sort of thing. How are you dealing with that?
segments.textZh: 嗯，但在过去几年里越来越不行了，你越来越成为一位公众人物、一位名人，现在你的名字开始出现在八卦版面和网站之类的地方。你是怎么应对的？

segments.textEn: I love it.
segments.textZh: 我喜欢。

segments.textEn: Is it interfering with your ability to do what you do?
segments.textZh: 这是否妨碍了你做自己所做之事的能力？

segments.textEn: I don't like it when people think wrong things. I mean, I'm like far from flawless, so I'm like. But I don't like when people think wrong things about me. And I guess the.
segments.textZh: 我不喜欢人们想些错误的事情。我的意思是，我远非完美，所以我就像是。但我不喜欢人们对我有错误的看法。我想这。

segments.textEn: I must say I don't really like the sort of celebrity element.
segments.textZh: 我必须说，我不太喜欢这种名人因素。

segments.textEn: I don't like when people sort of try to write things that are sort of trivialities that don't actually why I write about that. Obviously people find that kind of interesting or some people do, hopefully not many.
segments.textZh: 我不喜欢人们试图写些无关紧要的琐事，那些东西其实根本，为什么我要写那个。显然人们觉得那类事情很有意思，或者有些人觉得有意思，希望人数不多。

segments.textEn: And I don't know, sometimes people say wrong things that concerned that, well, what if my kids read that because they're five and they're starting to read and that's probably the most concerning thing. I'm not too worried about it from a business standpoint because most people that I interact with, particularly if they've known me for a while, they know what's true and what's not true.
segments.textZh: 我不知道，有时人们说些不实的话，让人担心的是，嗯，如果我的孩子读到了怎么办，因为他们5岁了，正在开始识字，这大概是最令人担忧的事情。从商业角度来说，我不太担心，因为与我打交道的大多数人，尤其是认识我已有一段时间的人，都知道什么是真的、什么不是真的。

segments.textEn: And in a lot of cases they don't care. Even if it was true, they don't care. But I do does concern me if my kids were to read something that was just not true.
segments.textZh: 而且在很多情况下，他们并不在意。即使那是真的，他们也不在意。但如果我的孩子读到某些完全不真实的东西，我确实会感到担忧。

segments.textEn: You understand? As Tesla continues to be successful and as SpaceX begins to assume the role of the space shuttle, you begin to become something like Henry Ford and Werner von Braun combined. And that's a level of celebrity few people ever know. And are you ready for that?
segments.textZh: 你明白吗？随着 Tesla 不断取得成功，以及 SpaceX 开始承担航天飞机的角色，你开始成为某种亨利·福特与沃纳·冯·布劳恩的结合体。那是很少有人体验过的知名度。你为此做好准备了吗？

segments.textEn: I'm probably not ready for that. I, I'm not a naturally extroverted person. In fact, I used to be horrendous at public. I mean, I'm not that great as it is, but I used to be really horrendous and just sort of shake and be unable to speak, but I kind of learned not to do that. So I mean, I'd much rather just be doing engineering and stuff and design. So that's really what I like to do and I'm happy to. And I like doing things like this which are, which are fine, but.
segments.textZh: 我可能还没为此做好准备。我，我天生并不是一个外向的人。事实上，我以前在公开场合糟糕透顶。我的意思是，我现在也没那么出色，但我以前真的糟糕透顶，只会有点发抖，连话都说不出来，不过我算是学会了不再那样。所以我的意思是，我更愿意只是做工程之类的事情，还有设计。这才是我真正喜欢做的事情，而我也乐于去做。我也喜欢做这种事情，这些，这些没问题，但是。

segments.textEn: And you know, if you're in the car business, you got to sell cars and stuff, so I got to go out there and be promotional. But there are other people at Tesla that actually are much better speakers and sellers of the car than I am, I think.
segments.textZh: 而且你知道，如果你从事汽车行业，就得卖车之类的，所以我必须走出去做宣传。但 Tesla 还有其他人实际上比我更擅长演讲和推销汽车，我觉得是这样。

segments.textEn: Well, that's hard to believe. Anything else you want to tell these folks out here?
segments.textZh: 嗯，这很难相信。你还有什么想告诉在场这些人的吗？

segments.textEn: Talked about a lot, I thought. There's some really good questions from the audience, actually.
segments.textZh: 我觉得已经谈了很多。实际上，观众提出了一些非常好的问题。

segments.textEn: Put your head down now.
segments.textZh: 现在低下你的头。

segments.textEn: I mean, I don't know.
segments.textZh: 我的意思是，我不知道。

segments.textEn: Wish us luck? I don't know. Something like that. I don't know. I mean, I'm not free, I'm not superstitious, but you never know. I mean, there could be some divine entity that sort of. There is. Then I hope that that entity is favorable.
segments.textZh: 祝我们好运？我不知道。诸如此类的话。我不知道。我的意思是，我不是自由的，我不迷信，但谁知道呢。我的意思是，可能会有某个神圣的存在，有点。确实有。那么我希望那个存在对我们有利。

segments.textEn: And worst comes to worst, you already know how to live on a dollar a day.
segments.textZh: 而且就算情况坏到极点，你已经知道如何靠每天1美元生活了。

segments.textEn: Yeah. Yeah, absolutely.
segments.textZh: 是的。是的，当然。

segments.textEn: Ladies and gentlemen, the uber entrepreneur, Elon Musk.
segments.textZh: 女士们、先生们，这位超级企业家，埃隆·马斯克。

segments.textEn: Elon, Mike, thank you so much for being here. We know that you have very busy schedules, both of you. We very much appreciate you taking time to speak with us this evening. And as a very small gesture of thanks, we have a wonderful Churchill Club T shirt for you. Please wear it in very good health and thank you all for coming. Look forward to seeing you at the next Churchill Club program. And by the way, there are 13 letters in Churchill Club.
segments.textZh: 埃隆、迈克，非常感谢你们来到这里。我们知道你们2位的日程都非常繁忙。我们非常感谢你们今晚抽出时间与我们交流。为了略表谢意，我们为你们准备了一件很棒的丘吉尔俱乐部T恤。请健康愉快地穿着它，也感谢各位的到来。期待在下一场丘吉尔俱乐部活动中见到各位。顺便说一句，Churchill Club有13个字母。

segments.textEn: Good night.
segments.textZh: 晚安。
